title: Minkowski's Theorem: Custom Lattice API vs ZLattice Comparison
description: A formal comparison between the custom Lattice API used in the parent Minkowski proof and Mathlib's ZSpan/ZLattice infrastructure. Proves the type equivalence Lattice n ≃ Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (Fin n → ℝ) with all lemmas complete: the round-trip identities and the key result that any basis matrix has nonzero determinant. The covolume bridge (equating L.covolume with the ZSpan fundamental domain volume) is described mathematically but not yet formalized.
keyResults: basis_matrix_det_ne_zero: (Matrix.of b).det ≠ 0 for any Basis (Fin n) ℝ (Fin n → ℝ) [proved]
latticeOfBasis: every Module.Basis gives a custom Lattice n [proved]
latticeEquivBasis: Lattice n ≃ Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (Fin n → ℝ) [proved]
covolume_eq_volume_fundamentalDomain: ENNReal.ofReal L.covolume = vol(ZSpan.fundamentalDomain (L.toModuleBasis n)) [not yet formalized — Lattice struct has no covolume field]
mathBackground: The custom Lattice type wraps a basis matrix with an invertibility condition. Mathlib's ZSpan approach abstracts this as Submodule.span ℤ (Set.range b) for a Module.Basis b. The central bridge is ZSpan.volume_fundamentalDomain, which shows vol(fundamentalDomain b) = ENNReal.ofReal |(Matrix.of b).det|.

overview.historicalContext: Minkowski's Theorem (1896) is the cornerstone of the geometry of numbers: any convex, centrally symmetric body in ℝⁿ with volume exceeding 2ⁿ times the covolume of a lattice must contain a nonzero lattice point. In formal mathematics, lattices admit several equivalent representations. Mathlib's canonical ZSpan approach models a rank-n lattice as the integer span of a Module.Basis, while our parent proof uses a more elementary custom Lattice type: an invertible n×n matrix. Both representations capture the same mathematical object, but proving their equivalence formally requires careful Lean 4 API work. This open question — whether the custom Lattice n and Mathlib's Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (Fin n → ℝ) are in canonical bijection — arose naturally during the formalization of Minkowski's theorem. Resolving it enables theorem transfer: any result stated in terms of the custom API can be exported to Mathlib's ZLattice/ZSpan framework, and vice versa.
overview.problemStatement: Is the custom `Lattice n` structure (an explicit invertible $n \times n$ matrix over $\mathbb{R}$) canonically equivalent to Mathlib's `Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (Fin n → ℝ)` (an abstract basis for $\mathbb{R}^n$ as an $\mathbb{R}$-module)? Formally, is there a bijection $\varphi : \text{Lattice}\, n \simeq \text{Basis}(\text{Fin}\,n,\, \mathbb{R},\, \mathbb{R}^n)$ whose forward map is `toModuleBasis` and whose inverse is `latticeOfBasis`?
overview.proofStrategy: The equivalence is established via two explicit conversion functions and a proof that they are mutual inverses. The forward map `toModuleBasis` (defined in the parent proof) sends a custom Lattice to a Module.Basis by using the matrix rows as basis vectors. The inverse `latticeOfBasis` (constructed here) wraps a Module.Basis back into a custom Lattice using the matrix `Matrix.of b`. The critical enabling step is `basis_matrix_det_ne_zero`: every basis matrix has nonzero determinant, proved via the change-of-basis product identity `det(b.toMatrix e) · det(Matrix.of b) = 1`. The round-trip identities then follow by reducing to matrix equality.
keyInsights: The entire equivalence hinges on a single key lemma: `basis_matrix_det_ne_zero`. For any `b : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (Fin n → ℝ)`, the matrix `Matrix.of b` (whose $(i,j)$-entry is $b(i)(j)$) has nonzero determinant. The proof uses the Mathlib identity `Basis.toMatrix_mul_toMatrix_flip b e = 1`, which gives $\det(b.\text{toMatrix}\,e) \cdot \det(\text{Matrix.of}\,b) = 1$, so $\det(\text{Matrix.of}\,b) \neq 0$.

Working in `Fin n → ℝ` (the product type) rather than `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` (the PiLp type) avoids module-instance complications. For the standard basis `e = Pi.basisFun ℝ (Fin n)`, each `e.repr` is definitionally the coordinate projection, making `e.toMatrix b = (Matrix.of b)ᵀ` provable by `simp`.

The round-trip identity for Module.Basis (`latticeOfBasis_toModuleBasis`) is proved by showing the two bases agree as matrices: `Matrix.of ((latticeOfBasis b).toModuleBasis n) = Matrix.of b`. Since `Matrix.of` is the identity on `Fin n → Fin n → ℝ`, matrix equality lifts to basis equality coordinate-wise via `DFunLike.ext`.

The `noncomputable` keyword on `latticeEquivBasis` reflects a mathematical subtlety: while the equivalence is canonical and its construction is explicit, `Lattice.toLinearEquiv` is built from `LinearEquiv.ofBijective`, which uses classical choice to extract a surjectivity witness. The equivalence exists definitively but is not decidably computable.

The natural completion of this API comparison — a formal proof that `ENNReal.ofReal L.covolume = λ(ZSpan.fundamentalDomain (L.toModuleBasis n))` — remains open because the custom `Lattice` struct has no `covolume` field. The bridge would use `ZSpan.volume_fundamentalDomain` together with `toModuleBasis_matrix_eq` to chain the determinant formulas.

sections.title: Setup and Open Question
sections.summary: File-level documentation stating the open question and its answer. Imports from Mathlib (ZLattice, InnerProductSpace, matrix determinant, Tactic). Namespace and variable declarations. The custom Lattice structure: a matrix together with a proof that its determinant is nonzero.

sections.title: Key Lemma: Basis Matrix Has Nonzero Determinant
sections.summary: Part 1. A helper lemma shows that for the standard basis e = Pi.basisFun ℝ (Fin n), we have e.toMatrix b = (Matrix.of b)ᵀ (proved by simp). The main lemma basis_matrix_det_ne_zero then uses the change-of-basis product identity to conclude det(Matrix.of b) ≠ 0 for any Module.Basis.

sections.title: Converse Conversion: Module.Basis → Lattice n
sections.summary: Part 2. Defines latticeOfBasis, which wraps a Module.Basis into a custom Lattice n by supplying basis_matrix_det_ne_zero as the invertibility witness. Completes the converse direction of the equivalence.

sections.title: Linear Equivalence and Module Basis Extraction
sections.summary: Part 3. Constructs Lattice.toLinearEquiv (a linear equivalence on Fin n → ℝ via transpose matrix multiplication) and Lattice.toModuleBasis (the forward map, via Pi.basisFun.map). Proves toModuleBasis_matrix_eq: the matrix of the resulting Module.Basis equals the original Lattice basis matrix.

sections.title: Round-Trip Identities
sections.summary: Part 4. Proves both round-trip identities: toModuleBasis_latticeOfBasis (the Lattice round-trip, by Lattice.mk.injEq and toModuleBasis_matrix_eq) and latticeOfBasis_toModuleBasis (the Module.Basis round-trip, by reducing to matrix equality via Matrix.of and DFunLike.ext).

sections.title: The Type Equivalence
sections.summary: Part 5. Packages the conversion functions and round-trip identities into latticeEquivBasis : Lattice n ≃ Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (Fin n → ℝ), the canonical answer to the open question. The noncomputable equivalence is the main theorem of this file.

conclusion.summary: The file fully proves `Lattice n ≃ Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ (Fin n → ℝ)`: the custom Lattice type used in the parent Minkowski proof is canonically equivalent to Mathlib's standard basis type. All five key results — basis_matrix_det_ne_zero, latticeOfBasis, the two round-trip identities, and latticeEquivBasis — are proved with zero sorries.
conclusion.implications: The equivalence validates the custom Lattice API as a mathematically sound and independently complete formalization of lattices in ℝⁿ. It enables theorem transfer: any result about the custom Lattice type (such as the main Minkowski theorem) can be restated in terms of Mathlib's ZSpan/ZLattice framework by transporting along latticeEquivBasis. The proof pattern — API equivalence via round-trip lemmas through matrix equality — is a reusable template for comparing different formalization strategies in Lean 4.
openQuestions: Can the covolume bridge be formalized? Specifically, is `ENNReal.ofReal |det L.basis| = λ(ZSpan.fundamentalDomain (L.toModuleBasis n))` provable using `ZSpan.volume_fundamentalDomain` together with `toModuleBasis_matrix_eq`? This would require adding a `covolume` field (or definition) to the custom Lattice type.

Does the full Minkowski theorem admit a clean Lean 4 proof purely in terms of Mathlib's `ZLattice` and `ZSpan.exists_ne_zero_mem_lattice_of_measure_mul_two_pow_lt_measure`, without reference to the custom Lattice type, once the API equivalence is available?
